title: Write a Production Dockerfile From Scratch
intro: The Docker tutorials had you building and debugging images. Now write the Dockerfile yourself — cache-friendly, non-root, and with a proper startup command.

steps.prompt: Write a Dockerfile for a Node app: base image node:20-alpine, working directory /app, copy package*.json first and run 'npm ci --omit=dev', THEN copy the rest of the source (COPY . .), run as the built-in 'node' user, expose port 3000, and start with CMD ["node", "server.js"] (exec form).
steps.hint: Order matters for the build cache: dependencies change rarely, source code changes constantly. COPY package*.json ./ → RUN npm ci --omit=dev → COPY . . means code edits don't re-run the install. CMD in exec form is a JSON array: CMD ["node", "server.js"].
steps.solution:
FROM node:20-alpine
WORKDIR /app
COPY package*.json ./
RUN npm ci --omit=dev
COPY . .
USER node
EXPOSE 3000
CMD ["node", "server.js"]
steps.fake_output:
[+] Building 14.2s (10/10) FINISHED
 => [3/5] COPY package*.json ./
 => [4/5] RUN npm ci --omit=dev
 => [5/5] COPY . .
 => naming to docker.io/library/app:latest
steps.explanation: A small, cache-friendly image that runs as an unprivileged user.
steps.why: Three habits in eight lines: dependency install before source copy (a code change rebuilds in seconds, not minutes — see docker-tutorial-006's layer history), USER node so a compromised app isn't root (docker-tutorial-010), and exec-form CMD so node runs as PID 1 and actually receives SIGTERM on 'docker stop' — shell form (CMD node server.js) wraps it in /bin/sh, which swallows the signal and forces a 10-second kill.
